**Setup.** Put O at the origin. Placing S = (0,0), A = (2,0), T = (3,√3), U = (2,2√3), R = (0,2√3), N = (−1,√3) and shifting by O = (−3,−√3) gives these vertices and distances from O:

| Vertex | Coordinates | Distance from O |
|---|---|---|
| S | (3, √3) | √12 |
| A | (5, √3) | √28 |
| T | (6, 2√3) | √48 |
| U | (5, 3√3) | √52 |
| R | (3, 3√3) | 6 |
| N | (2, 2√3) | 4 |

**Distance along the boundary.** The distance from O has its minimum at S (√12) and its maximum at U (√52). Going from S through A, T to U, it increases on every edge. Going from S through N, R to U, it also increases. Because the hexagon is convex, each circle of radius r centered at O with √12 ≤ r ≤ √52 therefore meets the hexagon in a single arc, of angular length L(r).

**Swept region.** Rotating that arc through 45° sweeps a contiguous arc of angular length L(r) + π/4. The swept area is therefore

Area = ∫ r (L(r) + π/4) dr = (area of hexagon) + (π/4) · (52 − 12)/2.

The hexagon has area (3√3/2)·4 = 6√3, and the second term is (π/4)·20 = 5π. So

Area = 6√3 + 5π ≈ 10.39 + 15.71 ≈ 26.10.
